title: One-time IPC listeners cannot be cleaned up before they fire
reasoning: The persistent listener API returns a cleanup function that removes the exact subscription, but the one-time listener API registers an anonymous wrapper and returns nothing. If renderer code installs a one-time listener for a channel and the component/request is cancelled or unmounted before the main process emits the event, that listener remains registered until a future event eventually fires. That can leak callbacks and can also deliver a stale event into a renderer flow that no longer owns the request.
recommendation: Mirror the `on` API shape for `once`: create a named subscription wrapper, register it with `ipcRenderer.once`, and return a cleanup function that calls `ipcRenderer.removeListener(channel, subscription)`.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for the preload IPC listener lifecycle, and the excerpt has no coverage demonstrating cancellation/unmount behavior for one-time listeners.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a preload IPC test with a mocked `ipcRenderer` that calls `window.ipc.once`, invokes the returned cleanup before any event is emitted, and asserts `removeListener` is called with the same channel and wrapper.
minimumFixScope: Change only `frontend/src/preload.js` listener registration for `once` and add a focused preload IPC lifecycle test.
